ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60 cm. It features a dark brown body with a distinct black-spotted head and a pale nuchal collar. It is distinguished by its large, dark eyes and numerous small teeth.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sibynophis sagittarius* is best distinguished by its distinct black head and nape collar, coupled with a series of small, paired black spots along the mid-dorsal line.
ai.habitat: Sibynophis sagittarius inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests across the Himalayan foothills and Northeast India, typically at elevations between 500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Cantor’s Black-headed Snake is primarily diurnal and actively hunts small lizards, often using its slender body to navigate through leaf litter in search of prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sibynophis sagittarius* is oviparous, laying small clutches of 3–4 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Sibynophis sagittarius occurs in the Himalayas and Northeast India, ranging from Himachal Pradesh to Arunachal Pradesh at elevations between 500 and 2,000 meters.
